products.name: Win32 App Uninstall & Removal Failure Remediation (Microsoft Intune) — Commercial
products.short_description: A branch-based diagnostic playbook and scripts for Intune Win32 app uninstall failures — intent conflicts, detection-gated removal, stale ProductCode (1605), wrong EXE switches (1603), app-in-use (1618), per-user vs SYSTEM context, supersedence, and IME log triage. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Make the uninstall actually uninstall — and prove the app is gone

You told Intune to remove a Win32 app and it did not come off. The console says Uninstall failed, or 1605, or it sits at Pending — or, worse, it reports the app as removed while it is plainly still on hundreds of machines. So the team retries, re-syncs, re-assigns, and finally deletes the app object to “force” it — stranding the software on every device that had not yet processed the removal. Removal is not installation in reverse: Intune’s Uninstall intent has its own delivery path, its own exit codes, and its own failure modes, and almost every one of them is invisible in the console.

This toolkit replaces guessing with a root-cause method built specifically for the removal path. It shows exactly how Intune processes an Uninstall intent — how it reconciles conflicting intents (Required silently beats Uninstall), how detection rules gate the removal on both ends (deciding whether the uninstall runs and whether it is judged successful), and how the Intune Management Extension runs the uninstall command and maps its exit code — then hands you a nine-branch tree that maps your exact symptom to the one cause that owns it.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths (Intune admin center > Apps > All apps > <app> > Properties > Program > Uninstall command); every group, filter, and evidence folder you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; comparable consulting runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every app you ever retire.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with four explicit removal gates: gone from the device, uninstall returned success, Intune agrees, and it stays gone.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — how Intune processes an Uninstall intent: intent reconciliation, detection-gated removal, exit-code mapping, and install context (SYSTEM vs user, HKLM vs HKCU).
  • Requirements Guide — the Intune roles, Graph scopes, device + IME-log access, and packaging record you need, each with how to verify it — plus the US Government (GCC High / DoD) targeting note.
  • Diagnostic Playbook — Step 0 fact-finding plus nine removal-failure branches (A–I): assignment intent conflict, detection-said-gone, detection loop, stale ProductCode (1605), wrong command/switches (1603), per-user vs per-machine context, app-in-use (1618) & reboot codes (3010/1641), supersedence removal, and reporting/lifecycle — each with symptom → why → exact fix → re-validate.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — on-device uninstall-readiness discovery (real ProductCode + registered uninstall string + cache + running processes), an assignment-conflict detector, a fleet uninstall-status reporter, an IME log parser for the uninstall sequence, and a guarded remediation (default preview) that corrects the uninstall command, generates a ProductCode-resolving wrapper, or re-syncs failed devices.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with the four pass/fail removal gates, plus Best Practices for authoring uninstall commands, detection rules, and unambiguous intents so removal works the first time.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each removal campaign feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next app retirement and the next project.

The bottom line

Every failed Win32 uninstall traced to its real cause — intent conflict, detection, ProductCode drift, command switches, install context, app-in-use, supersedence, or reporting — and fixed, with a repeatable method and scripts you keep and reuse.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as a single ZIP you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF & Word) — the complete, click-by-click solution: overview, requirements, the nine-branch removal playbook, testing & validation, troubleshooting, and best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting/log-parsing; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • APPUNIN-Discovery.ps1 — on the device, resolve the real MSI ProductCode, the registered uninstall string, HKLM vs HKCU registration, cached-MSI presence, and running processes/services
    • APPUNIN-Validation.ps1 — per-device uninstall/detection state mapped to the four gates, with assignment-conflict and supersedence-depth detection
    • APPUNIN-Report.ps1 — a fleet-wide removal report separating real failures from non-reporting devices
    • APPUNIN-LogParser.ps1 — parse the IntuneManagementExtension / AppWorkload / AgentExecutor logs for the uninstall sequence and exit codes
    • APPUNIN-Remediation.ps1 — guarded fix (default -WhatIf) that corrects the uninstall command, generates a ProductCode-resolving wrapper, or re-syncs failed devices

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts, in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
